Container.Name: OpenTools
Container.Overview:
568 document, image, audio, video, data and developer tools served from one container. Every tool runs in the browser tab that opened it: the file is read by the page and is never sent to the server, so this container serves the page and never receives the document. That makes it a static site to secure rather than a document processor - nothing to encrypt at rest, no retention period to set, no per-file audit trail.
Runs with no outbound network at all (verified with --network none): every page still serves and outbound requests fail to resolve, which suits an internal-only or air-gapped deployment.
Optional access gate: set both OPENTOOLS_AUTH_USER and OPENTOOLS_AUTH_PASSWORD and the instance asks for HTTP Basic credentials before serving anything. It is one shared credential for the whole instance, not user accounts. There is no TLS - put it behind a reverse proxy if you expose it beyond your LAN.
MIT licensed. Source: https://github.com/mgbuilderos/opentools

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the site is served on.

Config.Name: Page cache directory
Config.Description: Where the page cache is persisted. Optional - without it the cache simply starts empty after a restart.

Config.Name: Access gate username
Config.Description: Optional. Set this AND the password to require HTTP Basic credentials before anything is served. Setting only one fails closed.

Config.Name: Access gate password
Config.Description: Optional. Use a long value. Credentials travel in clear text unless you terminate TLS in front of this container.
